item.title: Firefighters extinguish forklift blaze in Wisbech
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Firefighters extinguish forklift blaze in Wisbech
Fire crews from Wisbech were called to a vehicle fire in the early hours of this morning. Firefighters arrived at Cromwell Road at 1:11 am to find a forklift alight. The team used a hose reel to put out the flames and had the incident under control by 1:58 am. Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service has confirmed that the cause of the fire was accidental.

item.title: Nominations open for 2027 West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Nominations open for 2027 West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards
Nominations are now being accepted for the 2027 King’s Lynn and West Norfolk Mayor’s Business Awards. Businesses and individuals have until 5pm on Friday, November 27, to submit entries across 11 categories, including the Champions in Agriculture award. The event, which celebrates local innovation and leadership, will culminate in a ceremony at the Alive Corn Exchange in King’s Lynn on Friday, March 5.
Organisers are seeking entries from a wide range of sectors, from farming to technology. Judges will also select an overall Mayor’s Business of the Year from the category winners. Each business is permitted to enter up to two categories. Further details on the awards and the full list of sponsors are available online.

item.description:

Apple Day celebrations taking place in Wisbech this Saturday
The Fenland Orchard Project is hosting an Apple Day celebration this Saturday at its Lynn Road site in Wisbech. The event runs from 2pm until 6pm and features a programme of live music, including performances from Treyes, Misfit Molly, Ady Bull, and Rusty Relics. Visitors can also watch demonstrations of traditional crafts such as willow and corn weaving, spinning, and sign writing.
Organisers are advising attendees to check the weather forecast before travelling, as rain is possible. Guests are encouraged to wear suitable footwear and bring waterproof clothing. As sunset is expected at 5:46pm, those planning to stay until the end of the event should bring a torch.

Royal British Legion donates commemorative bench to King’s Lynn care home
Residents at a King’s Lynn care home have received a new garden bench dedicated to forces veterans. The King’s Lynn branch of the Royal British Legion funded the inscribed seat through local fundraising efforts.
Branch chairperson Gerry Tann officially unveiled the bench at the Kettlewell Lane home during an afternoon tea event. The presentation was organised by staff members Jo Tayler and Julie Godfrey. Veterans living at the home, including John, Cyril, Ken and Bernie, joined Legion representatives to share stories about their time in the armed forces. The new addition is now available for residents to enjoy in the care home’s gardens.

item.title: Volunteers help create new wildflower meadow in King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Volunteers help create new wildflower meadow in King’s Lynn
Volunteers have joined West Norfolk Council staff to plant hundreds of native wildflower plugs at the Fairstead recreation ground in King’s Lynn. The project aims to transform the site into a diverse meadow to support local wildlife, including bees and butterflies. This work follows the earlier spreading of green hay to introduce native seeds to the area.
The initiative is part of the council’s Pollinator Action Plan, which seeks to restore habitats across the borough. Officials say the lessons learned at the Fairstead site will help guide future nature recovery projects in West Norfolk. The council has thanked the Nature Volunteer Network for their assistance in establishing this new green space for the community.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/volunteers-help-plant-wildflower-meadow-9488093/

Weasenham Lane in Wisbech reopens following water main repairs
Drivers in Wisbech can once again use Weasenham Lane. The road has reopened following repairs to a burst water main that had forced a closure for several days.
Anglian Water confirmed that while the pipework was fixed earlier, the route remained shut to allow for necessary repairs to the road surface. The route is now operating as normal.

Police appeal following assault on 505 bus
Lincolnshire Police are investigating an assault that took place on a 505 bus travelling between King’s Lynn and Sutton Bridge. Officers were called to Bridge Road in Sutton Bridge shortly after 6:05pm on Tuesday, October 20.
Reports indicate a man behaved aggressively towards a girl on the service before tipping alcohol on her, pulling her hair, and removing her from her seat. A second girl was also assaulted during the incident. Police are urging anyone who was on the bus at the time to come forward. Witnesses should contact 101 and quote incident number 404 of October 20.

A 46-year-old woman from West Winch is due to appear in court following an arrest at King’s Lynn bus station. Paula Asker, of Coronation Avenue, has been charged with being drunk and disorderly. Police were alerted to the incident by CCTV operators at approximately 5pm on Tuesday.
The charge comes as part of an ongoing effort by West Norfolk Police to tackle anti-social behaviour at the site. Officers have confirmed that Ms Asker has been bailed to appear at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, November 19. Police are continuing to monitor the area and are encouraging members of the public to report any concerns by calling 101, or 999 in an emergency.

Fenland students prepare for national skills competition
Students from across the Fens have been recognised at a special event ahead of the WorldSkills UK national finals. Learners from March, Terrington St John, and Wisbech are among those representing the College of West Anglia in the competition, often described as the skills Olympics.
The celebration at the King’s Lynn campus honoured students who progressed through regional heats to reach the finals this November. Local competitors include Erika Rimkus, Finn Mcauley, and Paige Marshall from Wisbech, Marc Watson from March, and Rianna Moore from Terrington St John. College principal David Pomfret praised the finalists, noting that they represent the top five percent of entrants in their respective vocational fields.

item.title: Looking back at October community events in the Fens
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at October community events in the Fens
We are taking a look back at community highlights from across the region during past Octobers. In 2017, King’s Lynn hosted a Halloween Spooktacular at the Vancouver Quarter, while young artists were celebrated at Gaywood Library’s superhero drawing competition. That same year, a 24-hour spinathon at Lynnsport raised over one thousand pounds for the British Heart Foundation.
Looking further back to 2013, the Railway Arms in Downham Market was named the national cider pub of the year. Meanwhile, in Swaffham, the cemetery chapel was rededicated following a forty-five thousand pound renovation. These stories reflect a busy period of local activity, from charity fundraising and remembrance services to community celebrations held across our towns.

item.title: King’s Lynn ambulance station hosts stem cell donor event
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn ambulance station hosts stem cell donor event
Staff and volunteers at the King’s Lynn ambulance station are holding a stem cell swabbing event this Monday. The initiative aims to find a donor for Reuben, the ten-month-old son of a local paramedic, who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia. The East of England Ambulance Service is hosting the session to encourage more people to join the DKMS stem cell register.
Those aged between 16 and 55 can participate in the simple cheek swab test. Members of the public who are unable to attend the station can also support the appeal by requesting a home testing kit through the DKMS website. Every new registration increases the potential for finding a life-saving match for patients in need of a transplant.

Students from across the Fens have attended a special event at the College of West Anglia’s Green Skills Academy in Wisbech. The "Girls in STEM" day aimed to inspire young women to consider careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
Pupils from Thomas Clarkson Academy in Wisbech and Neale-Wade Academy in March joined college students for practical activities, including virtual welding and thermal imaging. Organisers say the event was designed to challenge traditional gender stereotypes and highlight the growing need for a diverse workforce in sectors supporting a greener economy.

Nine new bus shelters installed across King’s Lynn
Nine new bus shelters have been installed in and around King’s Lynn following an £82,500 replacement programme. The project, funded by West Norfolk Council and a Norfolk County Council grant, replaces ageing structures that had suffered from damage and structural issues.
New shelters are now located on Winston Churchill Drive, William Booth Road, Gayton Road, Saddlebow Road, Queen Mary Road, and Parkway. Officials say the modern replacements are expected to last for 25 years. By removing advertising and electrical connections from the previous sites, the council expects to recoup its investment within four and a half years.
